newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Koor shareholder rejects spin-off plan.
newsitem.headline: Koor shareholder rejects spin-off plan.

text.p: A leading shareholder in Koor Industries Ltd said on Friday he opposed a plan to spin off parts of the holding company and said he expected Koor's share price to rise sharply in the next 18 months.
"There's a group that wants to break it up, but I think if one is patient you'll make more money by not breaking it up," Seth Glickenhaus, a U.S. fund manager, told Reuters in Jerusalem.
He said he expected to see Koor's New York Stock Exchange-listed ADRs at $30 within two years, compared with Thursday's closing of $19 15/16.

"Koor's stock has an aburdly low multiple and this will be recognised in the next year and a half," said Glickenhaus, whose Glickenhaus & Co manages more than $5 billion in assets. Glickenhaus holds about 1.5 million shares in Koor, or a little under three percent.

Glickenhaus was responding to a proposal made by Koor's chairman Stanley Gold last week. Gold, president of Koor's second-biggest shareholder Shamrock Holdings Ltd, said he wanted to spin off Koor's biggest publicly traded subsidiaries to shareholders.
The spin-offs would include Tadiran Ltd and Makhteshim Chemicals Works Ltd.
Israel's biggest holding company, Koor has interests in telecommunications and electronics, agro-chemicals and building materials.
Glickenhaus said he doubted Gold, who controls about 20 percent of Koor, would be able to win the board's approval for the plan. "In my opinion he won't be able to get a majority," he said.

Koor's biggest shareholder, Israel's Bank Hapoalim, has not commented on the proposal but bank officials said they would not act on it until Hapoalim itself was sold. The state-owned bank is in the process of being privatised by a tender due to be completed in mid-August.
Glickenhaus blamed Koor's lacklustre share price performance principally on a deteriorating political environment in Israel.
"I feel Israel overall has a much above average growth profile. Compared with other countries (it is) more business oriented and had a strong growth record in 1990-1995," he said.
